$comment: Drives two scripts. bootstrap.sh writes AWS SSO profiles into ~/.aws/config; tunnel.sh opens the SSM tunnels. Environments reference profiles BY NAME, so tunnel.sh never needs account/role details directly. Replace every placeholder (myorg, myproject, account IDs, sso_start_url, domain_suffix) with your own.

defaults.$comment_sso: Details for the [sso-session <name>] block bootstrap.sh writes. Skip bootstrap entirely if you use plain IAM profiles — just make sure each env's profile below already exists in ~/.aws/config.
defaults.$comment_bastion: How tunnel.sh finds the jump host: it looks up a running EC2 instance whose Name tag equals this template with {env} substituted. Must match the ssm-jumphost module output (<project>-<env>-ssm-bastion).

$comment_profiles: bootstrap.sh creates one profile per (account, role) pair. Name = profile_name_template with {account} (key from accounts) and {role_short} (from roles[]). Defaults below produce e.g. myorg-dev-admin, myorg-prod-admin.
$comment_environments: tunnel.sh reads this. Each env references a profile BY NAME (must exist in ~/.aws/config). Every resource is opt-in via enabled. Discovery is name/tag based — the first matching resource whose identifier contains the env name wins.

eks.$comment: Discovered via aws eks list-clusters; first cluster whose name contains the env name wins. Writes a kubeconfig context at ~/.kube/config-tunnel.

internal_alb.$comment_tags: Tag-based discovery. {env} is substituted. Any one tag set matching wins.
internal_alb.$comment_sni: If sni_hosts is empty, tunnel.sh reads the ALB listener host-header rules and routes each via HAProxy SNI.

aurora.$comment: Aurora cluster endpoint via describe-db-clusters; first cluster whose ID contains env name wins.

rds_proxy.$comment: RDS Proxy via describe-db-proxies; first proxy whose name contains env name wins.

redis.$comment: ElastiCache Serverless (Redis/Valkey) via describe-serverless-caches. Direct local port, no HAProxy.
